name: Dodo
overview: Dodo was a male figure identified as an Ahohite, notable primarily as the father of Eleazar, one of King David's mighty men. His tribal affiliation is not specified beyond this designation. The biblical record does not provide additional personal details or notes about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Dodo means 'beloved' and is a proper name mentioned in Scripture. This name is not indicated to be given directly by God, but it reflects a meaningful Hebrew name as recorded in 2 Samuel 23:9.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Dodo was the father of Eleazar, who is distinguished as one of David's mighty men. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Dodo's significance in the biblical narrative is primarily through his son Eleazar, one of David's elite warriors. Being identified as an Ahohite situates him within the broader context of David's military leadership. Although Dodo himself is not a central figure, his mention underscores the heritage and lineage of David's mighty men.
